body:
DRDO's place in India's defence system

The Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) is India's principal government organisation for defence research and development, functioning under the Ministry of Defence. It develops technologies and systems in cooperation with the armed forces, public-sector enterprises, private industry and other institutions.

Development, manufacture, evaluation and operational use are different responsibilities. DRDO may develop a missile; a production partner such as Bharat Dynamics Limited may manufacture it; the armed forces evaluate, accept and operate systems according to their requirements. Bharat Dynamics Limited and Bharat Electronics Limited are defence public-sector enterprises, not DRDO laboratories.

The Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme

The Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme (IGMDP) began in 1983. It sought to develop several important guided-missile capabilities through a coordinated Indian research effort. An official Ministry of Defence statement dated 13 August 2012 records that the programme was completed in March 2012.

The original programme covered 5 named projects. Their types and intended roles are fundamental examination facts.

IGMDP missileType or roleImportant historical distinction
PrithviSurface-to-surface ballistic missile.Developed into an inducted missile series.
AgniBallistic missile and re-entry technology demonstrator in the original programme.The demonstrator contributed to the subsequent Agni missile family.
AkashSurface-to-air missile.Developed into an operational air-defence system.
NagAnti-tank guided missile.Associated with fire-and-forget anti-armour technology.
TrishulLow-level surface-to-air missile project.Concluded as a technology demonstrator rather than an operationally inducted missile system.

Remember the original 5: Prithvi, Agni, Akash, Nag and Trishul. BrahMos, Astra and Nirbhay are important Indian missile programmes, but they were not among these 5 original IGMDP projects.

Why Trishul's status is different

The term technology demonstrator describes a project used to establish or evaluate technological capability. It does not necessarily mean that a weapon system was accepted for operational use. The Ministry of Defence's 2012 account specifically identified Trishul as completed in this form.

Similarly, the original Agni project was described as a re-entry technology demonstrator. This should not be confused with the later operational Agni missile family.

Important DRDO laboratories and locations

InstitutionLocationBroad association
Defence Research and Development Laboratory (DRDL)Hyderabad, TelanganaMissile research and development.
Research Centre Imarat (RCI)Hyderabad, TelanganaMissile avionics, guidance and related systems.
Advanced Systems Laboratory (ASL)Hyderabad, TelanganaStrategic missile technologies.
Integrated Test Range (ITR)Chandipur, Balasore, OdishaMissile flight testing and range measurements.
Terminal Ballistics Research Laboratory (TBRL)ChandigarhTerminal ballistics research.
Aeronautical Development Establishment (ADE)Bengaluru, KarnatakaAeronautical systems and cruise-missile development.
Gas Turbine Research Establishment (GTRE)Bengaluru, KarnatakaGas-turbine and related propulsion research.

DRDL, RCI, ASL, TBRL and ITR are identified together within DRDO's Missiles and Strategic Systems cluster. Other DRDO laboratories contribute according to the technology required by a project.

Prelims focus

  • IGMDP started in 1983 and was completed in March 2012.
  • The original projects were Prithvi, Agni, Akash, Nag and Trishul.
  • Trishul concluded as a technology demonstrator.
  • DRDL, RCI and ASL are associated with Hyderabad.
  • ITR is at Chandipur, Balasore, Odisha.
  • Trap: BrahMos, Astra and Nirbhay were not original IGMDP projects.

[Sources: Ministry of Defence, Press Information Bureau, 'Missile Development Programme', 13 August 2012, parliamentary reply; DRDO, 'Missiles and Strategic Systems', cluster and laboratory directory, consulted 14 November 2026; Ministry of Defence, Press Information Bureau, 'Indigenous Technology Cruise Missile successfully flight-tested', 18 April 2024.]

pictures.alt: IGMDP ran from 1983 to March 2012 with 5 original projects; BrahMos, Astra and Nirbhay were separate programmes outside the original IGMDP.

title: DRDO, Its Major Missile Laboratories and the Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme

body:
The Agni ballistic missile family

Agni is India's principal family of strategic ballistic missiles. Different variants have different ranges and characteristics. They should not be treated as a single missile with one fixed range.

Agni-1 is officially described as a short-range ballistic missile. The Strategic Forces Command conducted a successful test launch on 22 May 2026. Agni-4 was officially described as a medium-range ballistic missile in the announcement of its successful test on 6 August 2026.

Agni-Prime is a newer ballistic-missile development within the wider Agni family. In September 2025, an intermediate-range Agni-Prime missile was successfully launched from a rail-based mobile launcher. The significance for prelims preparation is its association with the Agni ballistic-missile family, not the mechanical details of the launcher.

What is MIRV?

MIRV stands for Multiple Independently Targetable Re-entry Vehicle. It refers to a ballistic-missile capability involving multiple re-entry vehicles that can be directed towards different targets. It is distinct from simply carrying one re-entry vehicle.

India's Mission Divyastra test in March 2024 demonstrated MIRV technology with Agni-5. A further official announcement dated 9 May 2026 reported a successful flight trial of an advanced Agni missile with a MIRV system conducted on 8 May 2026. The 2026 announcement did not identify a new missile called Agni-6; claims assigning an unannounced designation or range to that test should not be treated as official facts.

Prithvi: a surface-to-surface ballistic missile

Prithvi is one of the original IGMDP projects and developed into an inducted short-range ballistic missile series. Its core identity is surface-to-surface ballistic missile, not surface-to-air missile.

On 17 July 2025, Prithvi-II and Agni-I were successfully test-fired under the Strategic Forces Command. These were tests of ballistic missiles, not demonstrations of surface-to-air interception.

BrahMos: a supersonic cruise missile

BrahMos is a joint India-Russia missile programme involving India's DRDO and Russia's NPO Mashinostroyenia. The cooperation began through a joint-venture arrangement in 1998.

BrahMos is a supersonic cruise missile, not a ballistic missile. Its variants have been developed for launch from different platforms, including land, ships and aircraft, and for engagement of land or maritime targets. It uses ramjet technology during sustained cruise.

The system has been inducted into the Indian armed forces. A successful air-launched test from a Su-30MKI aircraft on 8 December 2021 was an important milestone for the air-launched version.

Nirbhay and indigenous cruise-missile development

Nirbhay is an Indian long-range subsonic cruise missile programme. DRDO reported successful development flight trials, including one on 15 April 2019. Its sustained atmospheric flight distinguishes it from ballistic missiles such as Agni.

The names Nirbhay, Indigenous Technology Cruise Missile (ITCM) and Long Range Land Attack Cruise Missile (LRLACM) appear in separate official announcements. They belong to the broader area of indigenous cruise-missile development, but their announcements should not automatically be treated as proof of identical configurations or identical induction status.

  • ITCM: Successfully flight-tested on 18 April 2024 with indigenous propulsion developed by GTRE, Bengaluru.
  • LRLACM: Successfully flight-tested on 15 June 2026; ADE, Bengaluru, was identified as the nodal laboratory.

Pralay: a quasi-ballistic missile

Pralay belongs to a different category from the subsonic cruise missiles just described. DRDO calls it quasi-ballistic. On 5 November 2026, a successful test was conducted as part of user evaluation trials. The official release stated that the system's induction had become imminent. This means the release reported progress towards induction, not completed induction.

ProgrammeCore categoryPublicly reported status or event
Agni familyStrategic ballistic missilesOperational family; Agni-1 test on 22 May 2026 and Agni-4 test on 6 August 2026.
PrithviShort-range ballistic missile familyInducted series; Prithvi-II test on 17 July 2025.
BrahMosSupersonic cruise missileInducted; developed through India-Russia cooperation.
NirbhaySubsonic cruise missile developmentSuccessful development flight trial on 15 April 2019.
ITCMIndigenous cruise-missile technologySuccessful flight test on 18 April 2024.
LRLACMLong-range land-attack cruise missileSuccessful flight test on 15 June 2026.
PralayQuasi-ballistic missileUser evaluation test on 5 November 2026; induction described as imminent.

Prelims focus

  • Mission Divyastra is associated with Agni-5 and MIRV technology.
  • Agni-1 is a short-range ballistic missile; Agni-4 is a medium-range ballistic missile in the 2026 official test announcements.
  • BrahMos is a supersonic cruise missile developed through India-Russia cooperation.
  • Nirbhay and ITCM are associated with subsonic cruise-missile development.
  • Pralay is quasi-ballistic; its 5 November 2026 announcement described user evaluation trials.
  • Trap: A successful test does not necessarily establish that the tested variant has been inducted.

[Sources: Ministry of Defence, Press Information Bureau, 'Missile Development Programme', 13 August 2012; 'Successful test-firing of Prithvi-II and Agni-I Ballistic Missiles', 17 July 2025; 'Successful test-launch of Agni-1 Ballistic Missile', 22 May 2026; 'Agni-4 Ballistic Missile successfully test-fired', 6 August 2026; 'India conducts successful flight-trial of Advanced Agni missile with Multiple Independently Targeted Re-Entry Vehicle system', 9 May 2026; 'Air version of BrahMos supersonic cruise missile successfully test-fired', 8 December 2021; 'Successful Trial of Nirbhay Sub-Sonic Cruise Missile', 15 April 2019; 'Indigenous Technology Cruise Missile successfully flight-tested', 18 April 2024; 'DRDO conducts successful flight-test of Long Range Land Attack Cruise Missile', 15 June 2026; 'DRDO conducts successful flight-test of quasi-ballistic missile Pralay', 5 November 2026. Official releases consulted 14 November 2026.]

body:
Akash: an indigenous surface-to-air missile system

Akash is an Indian surface-to-air missile system developed by DRDO. Its purpose is air defence: engaging aerial threats using missiles launched from the ground.

The established Akash system has a publicly reported range of about 25 km. This figure refers to the earlier Akash system and should not automatically be applied to every subsequent variant.

Akash has been inducted into the Indian Army and Indian Air Force. Its operation involves more than a missile alone: radar, command and control, launch equipment and supporting systems are also part of the weapon system.

Akash Prime and Akash-NG

Akash Prime is an upgraded version of Akash with an indigenous radio-frequency seeker and adaptations for particular operational requirements. On 16 July 2025, a successful first-of-production-model firing trial was conducted at high altitude in Ladakh. The Ministry of Defence's announcement on 17 July said that the trial would support timely induction. It did not state that this specific production variant had already completed induction.

Akash-NG means Akash Next Generation. It is a newer air-defence system with an indigenous radio-frequency seeker, a solid rocket motor and associated radar and command-and-control components. On 23 December 2025, DRDO announced successful completion of its User Evaluation Trials (UET). The announcement said this paved the way for induction; the statement should not be rewritten as confirmation that induction had already occurred.

Astra: an air-to-air missile

Astra is an Indian beyond-visual-range air-to-air missile (BVRAAM). It is launched from an aircraft to engage an aerial target. It is therefore distinct from the ground-launched Akash surface-to-air missile.

The Ministry of Defence has identified Astra among indigenous systems added to the Indian Air Force's inventory. On 11 July 2025, DRDO and the Indian Air Force reported successful tests of an Astra missile fitted with an indigenous radio-frequency seeker. That announcement described the tested system's range as exceeding 100 km. The figure should not be assumed to apply unchanged to every past or future Astra variant.

Nag: an anti-tank guided missile

Nag is a fire-and-forget anti-tank guided missile developed to engage armoured ground targets. The name should not be confused with a surface-to-air missile merely because both categories are guided weapons.

In January 2025, DRDO reported successful field evaluation trials of Nag Mk 2, a third-generation anti-tank guided missile, together with evaluation of its associated missile carrier. The Ministry of Defence described the complete system as ready for induction. The distinction between readiness and completed induction remains important.

Trishul: an important IGMDP distinction

Trishul was an original IGMDP low-level surface-to-air missile project. The government described it as completed in the form of a technology demonstrator. It should not be grouped with inducted systems merely because it was part of the original IGMDP.

Other Indian air-defence developments

  • VSHORADS: Very Short-Range Air Defence System, an indigenous man-portable system. DRDO reported 3 successful user-validation flight trials on 27 February 2026 and stated that induction could follow.
  • QRSAM: Quick Reaction Surface-to-Air Missile. It is an indigenous surface-to-air development associated with mobile, responsive air defence.
  • MRSAM: Medium-Range Surface-to-Air Missile, associated with India-Israel cooperation and inducted Indian air-defence capability.
  • Kusha: An indigenous long-range surface-to-air missile development. DRDO announced its maiden flight test on 23 July 2026. A maiden test is a development milestone, not evidence of completed induction.

Prelims focus

  • Akash is surface-to-air; Astra is air-to-air; Nag is anti-tank.
  • The earlier Akash system has a publicly reported range of about 25 km.
  • Akash Prime was tested in Ladakh on 16 July 2025.
  • Akash-NG completed user evaluation trials in December 2025.
  • Kusha underwent its maiden flight test on 23 July 2026.
  • Trap: Trishul was a technology demonstrator, while Akash became an inducted missile system.

[Sources: DRDO, 'Akash' and 'Akash Prime' product descriptions, consulted 14 November 2026; Ministry of Defence, Press Information Bureau, 'Cabinet Approves Export of Akash Missile System', 30 December 2020; 'Missile Development Programme', 13 August 2012; 'Successful trial of Akash Prime at High-Altitude', 17 July 2025; 'DRDO Successfully Completes User Evaluation Trials of Akash-NG', 23 December 2025; 'DRDO and IAF conduct successful flight-test of Astra Beyond Visual Range Air-to-Air missile with indigenous Radio Frequency Seeker', 11 July 2025; 'Successful Field Evaluation Trials of Nag Mk 2', 13 January 2025; 'DRDO conducts successful flight-trials of Very Short-Range Air Defence System', 27 February 2026; 'DRDO conducts successful maiden flight-test of Kusha Long-Range Surface-to-Air Missile', 23 July 2026.]

pictures.alt: Timeline of Akash Prime, Akash-NG, VSHORADS and Kusha tests from July 2025 to July 2026, distinguishing test stages from induction.

title: Indian Air-Defence and Anti-Tank Missiles: Akash, Astra, Nag, Trishul and New Variants
